bug: actor drifted off-distribution under an effectively absent entropy regulariser
detail: Two defects. (a) SCALE: default_target_entropy() returns -20.0, the -dim(A) convention for ONE 20-active-dim action, while the alpha loss consumed a log-prob summed over all 30 chunk steps; the correct floor is -20*30 = -600, so the equilibrium sat 580 nats too high. (b) STRENGTH (the operative cause): alpha remained ~0.010 while Q was ~1.4, so the entropy term was ~1%% of the actor objective. The policy was effectively unregularised and the OFT head was driven off-distribution.

observed_collapse.note: actor loss improved monotonically while behaviour was destroyed -- exactly why selection must use behavioural metrics, not optimiser statistics
observed_collapse.interpretation: log-prob falling +57 -> -293 means the policy became MORE stochastic (drifting off-distribution), not tanh-saturated.

positive_signal: before the collapse SAC improved over the SFT baseline: reach 0.2->1.0, grasp 0.0->0.8, mean return -0.44->2.21 at 6900 env steps; training episode 0 reached the lift stage with 0.215 m displacement
fix: TARGET_ENTROPY = default_target_entropy() * action_horizon (-600.0); ALPHA_INIT 0.01 -> 0.05; ALPHA_LR 3e-4 -> 1e-3; ACTOR_LR 1e-5 -> 3e-6
scope: trainer only; retargeter, reward, scene, camera, normalization, action mask, SFT init and eval suite all unchanged
correction_to_first_diagnosis: An initial reading attributed the collapse to the alpha gradient being mis-signed by the scale error. That is wrong and was caught by the regression test: at the measured log-probs BOTH targets push alpha in the same direction (down). The scale error raises the entropy equilibrium but did not flip the sign; the operative cause is alpha magnitude, not sign.

ROOT_CAUSE_FINAL.finding: The SAC entropy target was UNREACHABLE by the bounded action distribution.
ROOT_CAUSE_FINAL.measurement: log-prob of the tanh-squashed, +/-2.2-rescaled 20-active-dim action is bounded BELOW at -13.68 (minimum interior, at std ~0.40; the tanh Jacobian raises log-prob at both smaller and larger std). The -dim(A) = -20 heuristic assumes an UNBOUNDED Gaussian and lies below that floor.
ROOT_CAUSE_FINAL.mechanism: alpha_loss = -alpha*(logp+target) has gradient -(logp+target), which is positive across the entire operating range when target < floor. So alpha falls monotonically, the entropy regulariser vanishes, and the actor is left unregularised.
ROOT_CAUSE_FINAL.evidence: both pilots: alpha 0.049 -> 0.039 monotonically while behaviour oscillated 0 <-> 1.0
ROOT_CAUSE_FINAL.fix: default_target_entropy() = -8.4 (reachable, std ~0.20); actor_logstd initialised to log(0.20) so training starts at the alpha equilibrium
ROOT_CAUSE_FINAL.verified: stand-in gradient check: alpha now RISES when the policy is too tight (0.0500 -> 0.0519)
ROOT_CAUSE_FINAL.supersedes: earlier entries in this file attributing the collapse to a -600 scale mismatch or to alpha magnitude alone; the scale error was real but secondary, and the sign was never flipped -- the target was simply unsatisfiable
